stŏlātus , a, um, adj. stola.
I. Lit., dressed in or wearing a stola: “mulieres,” Vitr. 1, 1
med.—Subst.: stŏlātae , ārum, f., = matronae, noble dames, matrons, Petr. 44, 18.—
II. Transf.: “pudor,” i.e. befitting a matron, Mart. 1, 36, 8 : Ulixes, Ulysses in petticoats, a jocose appellation of Livia on account of her cunning, Calig. ap. Suet. Calig. 23.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
